title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is working out the functional equation of L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves on a variety over a finite field (the 'cas géométrique'), with duality as the engine. The setting is X of dimension n over F_p (q written p), E a sheaf with Euler characteristic χ(E), and b_i = dim H^i_c(X,E). In general the functional equation reads L_{DE}(t) = δ(E)(−t)^{−χ(E)} L_E(t^{−1}), where δ(E) = ∏_i det(F | H^i_c)^{(−1)^i} and D is Verdier duality.

On this page he computes δ(E) in a special case. E is assumed pure of weight ρ, so that Frobenius eigenvalues on H^i have absolute value p^{(i+ρ)/2} (conjectural in 1962). The cohomology is also assumed Poincaré-symmetric, b_i = b_{2n−i} (X proper smooth, E^∨ ≅ E(ρ)).

Then log_p|δ(E)| = Σ(−1)^i ((i+ρ)/2) b_i = (ρ/2)χ + (1/2)Σ(−1)^i i b_i. Pairing i with 2n−i gives Σ(−1)^i i b_i = 2nΣ_{i<n}(−1)^i b_i + (−1)^n n b_n = nχ. Hence δ(E) = ε(E) p^{(n+ρ)χ(E)/2}, with ε(E) = ±1. The value is exact up to sign because the duality pairing H^i × H^{2n−i} → Q_ℓ(−n−ρ) forces det·det = p^{…}.

This yields (2): L_{DE}(t) = ε(E)(−p^{±(n+ρ)/2} t^{±1})^{−χ(E)} L_E(t^{−1}).

He then remarks: if E^∨ ≅ E(ρ) globally on X, then D(E) = E^∨(n)[2n] ≅ E(ρ+n)[2n] for smooth X of dimension n. He adds that it suffices to have this on the function field, since lisse sheaves on a normal X are determined by the generic π_1-representation. Hence Rf_!(DE) ≅ Rf_!(E)(ρ+n)[2n]. The shift [2n] is even, and the Tate twist rescales Frobenius eigenvalues, so L_{DE}(t) = L_E(p^{−(ρ+n)}t).

Combining the two gives the classical self-dual functional equation L_E(t) = ±(p^{(n+ρ)/2}t)^{−χ} L_E(1/(p^{n+ρ}t)). For E = Q_ℓ, ρ = 0 this is Weil's Z(1/(q^n t)) = ±q^{nχ/2}t^χ Z(t).
errors: Possible convention slip in (2). From L_{DE}(t) = δ(−t)^{−χ}L_E(t^{−1}) with δ = ε p^{(n+ρ)χ/2}, one gets (−p^{−(n+ρ)/2} t)^{−χ}, not (−p^{+(n+ρ)/2} t)^{−χ}. Only the former is consistent with the next lines and Weil's classical form. The image shows a crossed-out 1/t inside the bracket, suggesting Grothendieck was himself adjusting this exponent.

The computation of |δ| uses purity (Frobenius eigenvalues of absolute value p^{(i+ρ)/2}), i.e. the Weil conjectures, not proved in 1962. Strictly, only ε(E) up to sign follows from the duality pairing, given the symmetry assumption. The page does not flag this.

'Il suffit que ce soit vrai sur le corps des fonctions … géométriquement' is not quite sufficient as stated. A geometric isomorphism E^∨ ≅ E(ρ) only holds up to a twist by a character of Gal(F̄_p/F_p), which would alter the constant in the functional equation.

ideas.what: Functional equation of L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves via Verdier/Poincaré duality, with constant δ(E) = alternating product of determinants of Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's functional equation for L-functions of ℓ-adic sheaves (Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula + duality)
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Bourbaki exp. 279 (1964), 'Formule de Lefschetz et rationalité des fonctions L'; SGA 5; SGA 4½ (Deligne, Rapport)

ideas.what: Computation that δ(E) = ±p^{(n+ρ)χ/2} using weight ρ and Poincaré symmetry b_i = b_{2n−i}
ideas.modern_name: Absolute value of the epsilon/determinant factor for pure self-dual sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (for constant sheaf); Grothendieck/Deligne in general

ideas.what: D(E) ≅ E^∨(n)[2n] on smooth X, and a self-duality E^∨ ≅ E(ρ) checked at the generic point, giving L_{DE}(t) = L_E(p^{−(n+ρ)}t)
ideas.modern_name: Verdier duality for lisse sheaves; self-dual (orthogonal/symplectic) local systems

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine working-out of the standard Grothendieck functional equation in the self-dual pure case, matching the published Bourbaki talk and SGA 5 material. The only features of note are the explicit dependence on the (then conjectural) weights and a possible exponent-sign slip.
transcription_corrections: In (2), the bracket seems to read '(−p^{(n+ρ)/2} 1/t)' with the '1/t' struck through or overwritten, rather than plainly '(−p^{(n+ρ)/2} t)'.
'δ(E) = 8(E) p^{…}': the second symbol is an overwritten δ or ε, so the line reads δ(E) = ε(E)p^{(n+ρ)χ(E)/2}.
Before 'D(E) ≃' a crossed-out 'L_E' appears; the struck text after it is 'Ě ⊗ Q_ℓ(n)', before 'Ě(n)[2n]'.
The page is written on the verso of a Bourbaki La Tribu typescript (n° 57, 1962), which supports a dating of about 1962–63.
